briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Tax Fight Becomes a Campaign Issue as Rescheduling Clears a Court Test
briefs.top: Michigan operators got a jolt of political momentum this week as a gubernatorial candidate embraced repealing the 24% wholesale tax, while Detroit's cannabis culture scene threw a party for the state's best products. Nationally, a federal appeals court just upheld marijuana's Schedule III move and Compass Pathways' psilocybin data keeps building toward an FDA decision.

local.text: John James backs repealing wholesale tax — "John James, the Republican candidate in Michigan's governor's race, said he supports repealing the state's 24% wholesale cannabis tax."
Metro Times crowns 2026 cannabis award winners — "The Detroit Metro Times staff picked their favorite Michigan flower, rosin, vapes, prerolls, edibles, and dispensaries of the year."
Jars Cannabis beats a surveillance camera fight — "Jars Cannabis wins removal of Madison Heights Flock camera."

Fields Cannary preps Muskegon dispensary-restaurant hybrid — "Fields Cannary, a Muskegon development, is targeting a fall opening for its retail cannabis dispensary, with a full-service restaurant to follow."

Wholesale tax revenue trails projections, fueling repeal push — the 24% tax generated about $37 million in the second quarter of 2026 and roughly $34 million in the first—against an initial estimate of $105 million per quarter, giving operators and candidates like James a data point for rollback.

national.text: Court upholds medical marijuana's Schedule III move — "Reclassification opponents filed a lawsuit to stop medical marijuana's change in schedule, but that challenge was rebuffed this week in federal court."

Trulieve rings the NYSE bell as cannabis first — the company celebrated becoming the first U.S. plant-touching cannabis firm listed on a major exchange, reporting "Trulieve generated $109 million in cash flow from operations in the first half of 2026, ending the second quarter with $325 million in cash."

FDA sets a forward path for psychedelic drugs — the agency's new framework signals a REMS-forward posture for future psychedelic approvals, meaning certified treatment centers and trained therapist dyads for MDMA and psilocybin therapies.

Compass Pathways posts durable psilocybin depression data — the company's Phase 3 trial showed "39% of patients achieving a clinically meaningful response after two doses of psilocybin", an effect that held for months as it advances toward an FDA filing.

DEA leaves states waiting on rescheduling rules — California's cannabis regulator said the agency hasn't shown "any sort of interest" in guiding states through the Schedule III transition, even as it presses California for more program details.
